name: Folklore Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Folklore Ventures (folklore.vc; Folklore Ventures Pty Ltd, ABN 72 614 351 058, a corporate authorised representative of Folklore FS Pty Ltd, AFSL 553 201), an Australian early-stage VC firm backing Australian and New Zealand tech founders from its office at 16 Eveleigh St, Redfern NSW (an inner Sydney suburb). Alister Coleman (ex-ShippingEasy co-founder) launched it in 2014 as Tempus Partners; it rebranded as Folklore in 2021 (its 2017 Fund 2 post is now retitled 'Folklore Fund 2'). Its LinkedIn company page (linkedin.com/company/folklorevc) is linked from the site. Not 'The Folklore' / The Folklore Group (Amira Rasool's African fashion marketplace, which itself raised seed money), which shows up in database searches for this name.

open_items: No Melbourne office found. The site, FAQs and team pages give only the Redfern (Sydney) office; Alister Coleman grew up in Melbourne, and several portfolio companies (Arkeus, Swoop Aero, Uptick) are Melbourne-based, but no Folklore Melbourne presence is stated.
check_range currency is inferred as AUD: the FAQ writes '$2.5M' without a currency code on an Australian firm's site. No minimum is stated ('micro-cheques').

No application form or apply URL: founders are told to 'reach out' via a Get in touch button (a general hello@ mailbox, not recorded); an /office-hours page also exists. Cold inbound recorded as yes from the FAQ wording.
Indian founders: not stated anywhere; the firm describes its remit as Australian and New Zealand tech founders.

requires_us_entity = no is inferred, not stated: Folklore uses the Australian Investment Council's Open Source Seed Financing docs (Australian company documents) and backs Australian/NZ companies. Its toolkit reposts a DLA Piper Q&A on flipping to a US company, without a Folklore position.

portfolio_count_reported not recorded: the firm states no total. The companies page lists 29 companies plus 5 'Partner Direct Investments' (Oct 2026); the Octopusbot post calls it Folklore's '13th investment into an AI-native software startup'; WaveUp (database) says 22 investments; a 2020 Substack analysis said 14 portfolio startups.

Funds: Fund 1 size and close not found (only 'launched in 2015' in a third-party Substack analysis; SmartCompany says Forever Network was a 2015 first-fund investment). Fund 3 was 'already investing' in March 2021, but its size, final close and legal name were not found. Fund 2/3 ESVCLP status comes from WaveUp (database). Fund 2 currency AUD is inferred from the ESVCLP structure; its close date is the announcement month (~$20M first close earlier in 2017).

A '$350 million fund' raise backed by Brett Cairns (ex-Magellan; listed on Folklore's team page as Board) and Canva co-founder Cameron Adams appears only on WaveUp (database) and in a CB Insights search snippet; no press or primary page was fetched, so no Fund 4 was recorded and its status (target, closes) is unknown.

Rounds not recorded: Sphere's Nov 2025 Series A (Folklore's post says a US$20M a16z-led round; Sphere's blog and TechCrunch say $21M led by Andreessen Horowitz with YC and Felicis and do not name Folklore, whose stake dates from Sphere's/ScholarSite's first round); Forever Network's 2024 $6M Series A (SmartCompany says Folklore did not participate; Folklore's stake is from 2015).

Portfolio rounds without a fetched round page: Blunge (AI design agent, Brisbane; database hints of a Feb/Mar 2026 seed), ZenCheck (database hints of a Dec 2024 seed with Redstone VC), SUMM (formerly Crypto Tax Calculator), Komodo, Swoop Aero, Wonde, Auror, Kanopi, HealthMatch. Folklore has 'our-investment-in-…' posts for Komodo, Swoop Aero, Wonde, Visionary Machines, Canopy Study and ProductEngine that were not fetched (all pre-2023).

SimConverse seed amount not found on a fetched page: Business News Australia ('Folklore, Artesian back $1.5m seed round') returned 403; parsers.vc lists $1.5M dated Oct 2022 while Folklore's post is dated 2023-03-09.

Amounts not disclosed for Octopusbot (seed, Jul 2026) and oslo.ai (Mar 2024). Octopusbot's Grain Central page returned 403; HQ not stated for Octopusbot, oslo.ai, SimConverse or Lived. Hullbot also appears in Axios (headline 'raised $10.6M', presumably USD) and Capital Brief; not fetched.
Currencies for ProductEngine, Canopy Study, Visionary Machines 2025 and Lived are written '$' in Australian sources and recorded as AUD by inference.

Partner focus sectors are empty: the team page and partner profiles give titles and LinkedIn links only, with no sector coverage. Other investment staff: Divine Aaron and Orson Cairns (Investors), Mitchell Bissinger, Dan Fleming and Tanisha Banaszczyk (Investment Advisors); Dan Fleming was quoted on the ProductEngine and Canopy Study deals.

Stages: the firm describes itself as a first-cheque investor (96% of founders backed at pre-seed or seed, 2022), but its two most recent Series A entries (Hullbot, Arkeus) were new positions, so series_a is included.
